Author: bdg
Name: CWLS Go To
Description: Watches Cross-world Linkshell (CWLS1/CWLS2) chat for messages containing a map link and appends a clickable [Go To] link. Clicking it teleports you to the nearest aetheryte via the Teleporter plugin, hopping to the correct world/data center first via the Lifestream plugin if the message points to a different server. Also adds a Go To entry to the right-click menu of anyone whose whereabouts the game shows - party finder listings, party members, friends, free company, linkshell and cross-world linkshell - which teleports to the aetheryte in the zone they are standing in, changing world first if they are on another one.
Punchline: Adds a working [Go To] link to CWLS map-link messages.

Author: bdg
Name: Desynth All Command
Description: Adds a /desynthall command that opens the game's desynthesis (materia extraction) window and automatically desynthesizes every item in the list, confirming each dialog and closing each result, using the same technique as PandorasBox's Desynth All feature. Self-contained - PandorasBox is not required. Temporarily pauses Yes Already's own dialog handling if it's installed, to avoid it racing with the confirmation step.
Punchline: Opens the desynthesis window and desynthesizes everything in it.

Author: bdg
Name: Mod Guard
Description: Keeps your mods private: when a mod-sync plugin (Lightless, Snowcloak, Sphene, PlayerSync, or any Mare Synchronos fork - the watch list is editable) is loaded, Mod Guard hides all your Penumbra mods by force-assigning an empty temporary collection to your character, and reverts + locks your Glamourer state, so sync plugins have nothing to share. Once the sync plugins are gone (or on demand), it restores everything exactly as it was - your real Penumbra collection, mod settings, and captured Glamourer state are never lost. Hidden state never spans a logout: it is restored as you log out and re-hidden fresh right after the next login, because a hidden state that goes stale across a relog left the character black. Use /modguard to open the control window. Requires Penumbra; Glamourer optional.
Punchline: Hides your Penumbra mods and Glamourer state while mod-sync plugins are active.

Author: bdg
Name: Typo Guard
Description: On Latin American keyboard layouts, / is Shift+7, so a missed Shift sends "7artisan" into chat instead of running /artisan. Typo Guard intercepts outgoing chat and blocks any message that starts with a 7 followed by a letter, printing what it blocked instead of sending it. If you really meant to send such a message, send it again within 5 seconds and it goes through. Toggle with /typoguard (also accepts on/off/status); the setting persists.
Punchline: Blocks chat messages that start with 7 - mistyped slash commands.

Author: bdg
Name: Auto Lister
Description: Adds an 'Auto List' button next to Dagobert's 'Auto Pinch' on the retainer sell list. Clicking it goes through every marketable item shown in the bottom-right quarter of the inventory (the last display page, as sorted on screen), puts each up for sale, opens the price comparison, undercuts the cheapest matching HQ/NQ listing by 1 gil and confirms - until the quarter has no more sellable items or the retainer's 20 sell slots are full. Items whose listing would total under 2,000 gil (price x quantity), or whose vendor price beats the market proceeds after the 5% sales tax, are sold through the retainer instead of taking up a market slot. The price-checking logic mirrors Dagobert's auto pinch. A 'Pinch & Cull' button reprices the retainer's existing listings the same way, but listings whose new price falls under those thresholds are returned to your bags and vendored instead - and a 'Pinch & Cull All' button on the summoning bell's retainer list runs that across every retainer with listings.
Punchline: One-click bulk market listing and Dagobert-style repricing with automatic vendor culling.

Author: bdg
Name: Gem Rate
Description: Watches your Bicolor Gemstone count and shows a small window with the current total, how many you gained this session, your earn rate per hour (whole session and the last 15 minutes), and the estimated time until you hit the 1,500 cap. The session clock starts at your first gain so idle time before farming doesn't skew the rate. /gemrate toggles the window.
Punchline: Tracks how many bicolor gemstones you earn per hour.

Author: bdg
Name: Faloop Screener
Description: Logs into your Faloop account and shows the current S/SS-rank spawn windows in a table (/windows): world, hunt, zone, time open, window progress and cap time, computed from Faloop's live tracker state - accurate even for kills that happened while you were offline. Filter by world (Crystal data center), hide zones or specific hunts you don't care about, and click Spawn on any row to see that hunt's spawn trigger. Requires a Faloop account with tracker access; credentials are stored in the plugin config like Faloop Integration does.
Punchline: S-rank spawn windows from Faloop, filterable, with spawn conditions.

Author: bdg
Name: Hook Namer
Description: GatherBuddy Reborn can reuse your own AutoHook presets instead of generating its own, but only if a preset is named exactly the target fish's item ID (it compares the whole name, so "4948 Glimmerscale" will not match - it has to be "4948"). Community presets never follow that convention. Hook Namer reads your AutoHook presets, works out which fish each one targets, and creates an ID-named duplicate through AutoHook's import API, filed into a 'HookNamer' folder in AutoHook's preset list to keep things tidy - your originals are left untouched. Presets that target several fish, or none, are listed so you can pick the target yourself. Open with /hooknamer.
Punchline: Makes your AutoHook presets usable by GatherBuddy Reborn.

Author: bdg
Name: Hunt Tally
Description: Reads the game's hunt achievement list, fetches your live progress from the server (the same request the achievement window makes) and shows it grouped by expansion: every S-rank and A-rank kill-count achievement with a progress bar and how many kills remain, plus the big overall elite-mark totals. Progress is cached per character so the window opens instantly; refresh on demand. Open with /hunttally.
Punchline: How many S and A ranks you still need for each hunt achievement, per expansion.

Author: bdg
Name: Stack Splitter
Description: Adds a "Split into stacks of N" entry to the right-click menu of stackable inventory items. The stack (and any other bag stacks of the same item) is split until no stack holds more than N, leaving the remainder as the last stack. The size is configurable in the plugin settings (/stacksplitter), defaulting to 50.
Punchline: Right-click a stack to split it into stacks of your chosen size.

Author: perchbird (originally Meli), local music by bdg
Name: Orchestrion (Local Music)
Description:
Orchestrion Plugin allows you to change the currently playing in-game BGM. It includes
a curated list of the most accurate in-game song titles, so you know exactly what's playing,
if you want to know later! Add favorite songs to separate them from the rest.
This fork also plays your own music files: point it at a folder in the settings and the
tracks join the song list, mixable with game songs in playlists.
Note: This plugin does not currently allow you to play actual orchestrion songs.
Punchline: Browse and change the in-game BGM, with your own music files mixed in.
Changelog:
2.3.0.19:
Dungeon bosses were still slipping through: the roaming baseline was re-adopted from
any song that played five seconds out of combat, so the boss theme - which starts on
entering the arena, well before the pull - became the baseline itself and left nothing
to compare against. Inside a duty the baseline is now taken once, from the first
settled song, and frozen until the instance is left.

2.3.0.18:
Dungeon boss detection: the game does not keep the boss theme in the scene a playlist
overrides, so watching only that scene reported "no song" and nothing could ever be
compared. The zone and boss music are read from wherever the game actually puts them
now. Duty pulls also log every scene's song, so a fight that still slips through can
be pinned down from /xllog.
2.3.0.17:
Dungeon bosses are detected again while a playlist is playing. The scene holding the
zone/boss BGM is the very one a playlist overrides, so the boss theme was being
overwritten before anything could see it; what the game asks for is now recorded
before it gets replaced.
2.3.0.16:
Fixed dungeon boss detection: boss themes that start moments before the pull (door
seal, intro, cutscene) were poisoning the zone-music baseline, so the "music changed"
check never fired. The baseline now only adopts a song after 5s of out-of-combat
stability, and duty pulls log their detection state for troubleshooting.
2.3.0.15:
The playing playlist now skips to its next song whenever you change zones, like the
game's own BGM changing per area (toggleable in settings).
2.3.0.14:
New headphones button in the player/mini player: toggles whether music keeps playing
while the game window is in the background (it flips the game's own "Play sounds while
window is not active" + BGM settings, so game tracks and local files both follow).
Green while enabled.
2.3.0.13:
Volume normalization for local music: each file's loudness is measured during the scan
(cached per file; the whole existing library is analyzed on the first scan after this
update) and playback applies a per-track gain to bring everything to a common level,
capped so nothing clips. A new "local music level" slider aligns your files with the
game's BGM loudness; both settings apply live to the playing track.
2.3.0.12:
Auto-resume is now persistent: if the playlist can't start right after login (estate/inn
music active, zone still loading), it retries every 5s for up to a minute and logs what
happened instead of silently giving up.
2.3.0.11:
Local music now goes silent while the game window is unfocused, matching the game's
own audio - it honors "Play sounds while window is not active" and its BGM sub-toggle.
2.3.0.10:
Playlists now remember their repeat/shuffle modes across restarts (they used to silently
reset to Repeat One). The plugin also remembers the last playing playlist and resumes it
automatically after login (toggleable in settings); stopping playback via the player
clears the auto-resume.
2.3.0.9:
Entering combat now starts on a random song from the combat playlist.
2.3.0.8:
Coming out of combat now advances the normal playlist to its next song instead of
restarting the interrupted one, and the combat playlist continues from where the last
fight left off instead of starting over.
2.3.0.7:
Local tracks now fade out (~1.5s) when replaced or stopped, matching the game's own
BGM transitions - no more abrupt cut when combat music ends.
2.3.0.6:
New "Add to <playlist>" button in the All Songs / History footer: adds the selected
song(s) to the playing playlist, or the one selected in the Playlists tab. Supports
Ctrl/Shift multi-select.
2.3.0.5:
New fist button in the player/mini player: moves the current song out of the playing
playlist into the combat playlist and skips to the next.
2.3.0.4:
Combat music: pick a playlist that takes over while you fight - triggered by any combat,
by hunt marks (an engaged B/A/S rank nearby), and/or by duty bosses (trials and raids
from the pull, dungeon bosses when the boss theme starts). The previous playlist or the
game BGM resumes a few seconds after the fight ends.
2.3.0.3:
New "Everything playlist" button in the playlist pane: one click builds an "Everything"
playlist with every available song (local tracks included); clicking again adds only
songs that are new since last time. New trash button in the player/mini player removes
the current song from the playing playlist and skips to the next.
2.3.0.2:
Local music support: scan a folder of your own audio files (mp3, ogg, wav, m4a, aac, wma, flac)
and play them alongside game songs, including in playlists. Volume follows the in-game
master/BGM sliders.
2.3.0.1:
Fixed bug where Deep Dungeon mode would not switch tracks
2.3.0.0:
Long-awaited new feature, implemented by @NPittinger!
The Orchestrion plugin can now report the titles of songs played inside housing instances and inns by the Orchestrion furnishing.
Limitations:
- The plugin still cannot play Orchestrion rolls.
- Titles of songs played inside housing instances can appear in the server bar and in chat messages.
- Songs played inside housing instances will not appear in your listening history and cannot be added to playlists.
- Only English and Japanese titles are available for Orchestrion rolls, as those are the only languages provided by the game.

Author: bdg
Name: Laziness
Description: A window of one-click chores. "Buy soil" talks to Hismena in Idyllshire, spends your Allagan Tomestones of Poetics on Unidentifiable Shells, then walks over to Bertana and trades every shell for Grade 3 Shroud Topsoil. Stand near the NPCs and press the button.
Punchline: One button for the chores you keep putting off.

Author: bdg
Name: Gather Tally
Description: Shows the game's Miner, Botanist and Fisher achievement categories in three collapsible sections, each with a progress bar and how much is left. Progress is fetched from the server (the same request the achievement window makes) on demand with the Refresh button, per section or all at once, and an optional auto-refresh keeps the expanded sections ticking while you gather. Recent gains are marked so you can watch counters move. Cached per character. Open with /gathertally.
Punchline: Live progress on every miner, botanist and fisher achievement.

Author: bdg
Name: Artisan GBR Bridge
Description: Artisan only knows how to talk to the original GatherBuddy, and its check is simply whether a plugin called GatherBuddy is loaded - so this one carries that name to switch the greyed-out "Gather Item" entry back on. Clicking it now files the ingredient into a GatherBuddy Reborn auto-gather list named after the crafting list it came from, with the amount you are still missing; click more ingredients and they join the same list. Typing /gather or /gatherfish yourself is untouched and still goes straight to GatherBuddy Reborn. Requires Artisan and GatherBuddy Reborn; the original GatherBuddy must not be running.
Punchline: Sends Artisan's "Gather Item" into a GatherBuddy Reborn list.

Author: bdg
Name: Let Go
Description: Hold Shift and your current target is cleared; release it and the same target comes back. Useful when having something targeted gets in the way - placing a ground-targeted action freely, or keeping the camera and character from being pulled around - without losing your place in the fight. If you pick a new target while the key is down that choice is kept instead, and nothing happens while you are typing, so capital letters in chat leave your target alone. By default it only acts while playing a healer - the settings can open it up to every job. The key can be changed to Ctrl or Alt in the settings, which is worth doing if you use Shift as a hotbar modifier. Open the settings with /letgo, and switch the whole thing on or off with /lg - or /lg on and /lg off to set it outright from a macro.
Punchline: Drop your target while a key is held, take it back when you let go.

Author: bdg
Name: FATE Hopper
Description: Shows the active FATEs and critical encounters in the Occult Crescent - South Horn and North Horn - as a clickable list, like the one Vanilla Plus draws. Critical encounters sit on top in gold with their remaining recruitment time, and two fixed North/South buttons teleport you toward the pot FATE spawn points before they spawn, so you can be waiting when they do. A Buffs button runs the Freelancer errand: swap to Freelancer, press Inquiring Mind (every phantom buff at once), and swap back to the phantom job you were on - stand near the knowledge crystal for it. A Return button presses Return and accepts its confirmation - and only that one, armed solely by the button press, so the release prompt on death is never touched. Both errands also run as commands for hotbar macros: /fatehopper return and /fatehopper buffs, refusing to act outside the Occult Crescent. Clicking a FATE teleports you to the aetheryte shard nearest to it, through the Lifestream plugin - you have to be standing within range of any shard already, the same as using one by hand; the plugin picks the destination and does the clicking. The window opens by itself when you enter the zone and can be toggled with /fatehopper.
Punchline: Click an Occult Crescent FATE to shard-hop toward it.

Author: bdg
Name: Occult Coffers
Description: Cast Occult Treasuresight and this reads the count it reports - so many silver, so many bronze - then watches which coffer spawn spots you walk past. Every spot you come close to is one fewer place a coffer can be hiding, and the moment the spots you have not visited match the number still unaccounted for, those spots have to be the coffers, and they get marked on the map. Until then the unvisited spots are marked too, in a dimmer icon, so you can see at a glance which parts of the zone you have already swept. The spawn spots come from the zone's own layout data, so nothing has to be recorded by hand, and every coffer you find along the way is subtracted from the count. Works in South Horn and in North Horn, where markers are kept on the right floor - the North Basin and the Subterrane are separate maps and get separate marks. Drawn as its own layer on the map, so it does not fight with any other plugin's markers. Toggle it with /coffers.
Punchline: Narrows down where the Occult Crescent coffers are by elimination.

Author: bdg
Name: Glam Roulette
Description: Hands every other player around you a Glamourer design picked at random, so the world stops being a sea of the same three glamours. Glamourer can already do this to one person at a time - it matches automated designs to one exact character name, and its apply command takes a single target - so this walks the object table instead and does it to everyone. Each player keeps the outfit they were given: the choice is remembered against their name and world, so the same person looks the same tomorrow rather than reshuffling every time they walk back into view. Re-roll one person from the context menu on their name, or everyone at once with /glamroulette reroll. The design pool can be narrowed to a folder so it only draws from the designs you meant for this. It will also quietly turn every female Hrothgar into an Elezen if you would rather not look at them, which Glamourer cannot be told to do on its own because its rules match one named character rather than a race. Yourself is never touched, party members can be exempted, and everything it changed is reverted when the plugin unloads. All of it is local: this changes how other people look on your screen and nowhere else - they see themselves normally, and so does everyone else. Toggle the window with /glamroulette.
Punchline: Dresses everyone else in a random Glamourer design.

Author: bdg
Name: Mount Heels
Description: Simple Heels lifts you by whatever height your shoes declare, so they sit on the ground instead of sinking into it. Get on a mount you stand on top of rather than sit in and that lift goes away, because it has one "Mounted" offset shared by every mount in the game and a chocobo wants nothing. This gives each mount its own, and takes the height from the mods rather than from you: it reads the same number Simple Heels already worked out for the shoes you have on, so it follows a change of shoes on its own and there is nothing to dial in. Tick a mount while you are riding it and that is the whole setup; a trim for height, sideways, forward and turn is there for a platform that is not quite where the game says it is. Mounts you have not ticked are left entirely alone. Toggle the window with /mountheels.
Punchline: Heels that keep working on a mount you stand on.

Author: bdg
Name: Hunt Spots
Description: Draws the spots where A and S ranks come up onto the game's own map, in every zone from A Realm Reborn to Dawntrail. Open the map and they are there - browse to a zone you are about to fly to and they are there too, so you can see where to look before you arrive. Points that serve more than one rank are drawn once, as the rarest of them, with the ranks in the tooltip. Spawn points are not in the game files: nothing in the sheets says where a mark can appear. These are the ones the community mapped out, taken from Hunt Helper (github.com/img02/HuntHelper, MIT) and used with thanks - if you want to record or correct them, that is the plugin to do it in. Icons and size are configurable, and the defaults deliberately avoid the ones Eureka Linker uses. Toggle the window with /huntspots.
Punchline: A and S rank spawn points, on the real map.

Author: bdg
Name: CBT
Description: Tweaks that are sometimes simple, sometimes not.
Punchline: Yet another tweaks collection plugin.
